Brining rights are on the line at an upcoming pickling contest at a Langston Blvd barbecue spot. Sloppy Mama’s is hosting its second “pickle party” competition this Saturday from 2:30-4:30 p.m., inviting guests to vote on the quality of a brined bounty of pickled cucumbers, mangos and more. “We kind of took a shot in the dark with a pickle party last year, and it ended up being super popular,” Sloppy Mama’s owner Joe Neuman told ARLnow. “It’s more than just cucumbers. People don’t always know, but you can pickle a lot of things.” The event at 5731 Langston Blvd is a fundraiser for the Arlington Food Assistance Center (AFAC). It will feature two main categories — cucumber pickles and non-cucumber pickles — and upon entry, guests will receive two tokens to hand to their favorite from each category. Last year’s non-cucumber category featured foods such as watermelon rind, beans and the defending champion, turnips. Contestants’ creativity led Neuman to add a third category this year called, “You can pickle that?” Sloppy Mama’s will be the judge of that category. Flyer for “Pickle Party” at Sloppy Mama’s on Langston Blvd (staff photo by Ryan Cole) Registration is available online. General admission is free, but it will not include any food, drink or merchandise. A $60 ticket package includes all-you-can-eat pig roast, unlimited “Czexican” lager (a cross between Mexican lager and a Czech-style pilsner), novelty pickled food items and themed snacks. A VIP “Very Important Pickle” package, for $150, includes everything listed above, as well as a “swag bag” with stickers, koozies and a custom “Dilly Briny” T-shirt featuring the party’s pickle mascot. “He was inspired by David Bowie,” Neuman said of the snazzy pickle icon. “We have plenty of Dilly Briny merch, and it’s all pretty sweet.” Winners this year will receive a $100 Sloppy Mama’s gift card, as well as a year of free pickles from the restaurant. AFAC, the event’s beneficiary, is an Arlington nonprofit that provides food to community members experiencing food insecurity. “It’s really fun, but this all started because I really wanted to do a fundraiser with AFAC,” Neuman said. “I think what they do is important because they’re helping people that need some help, and it starts with food access.” About the Author Ryan Cole Ryan Cole is a reporting fellow at ARLnow and an Arlington native. He’s a 2022 Yorktown High School graduate and a 2026 graduate of Northwestern University, where he studied journalism and covered sports for campus publications. #Langston Blvd #party #restaurant

Share it with your friends! Facebook Twitter Google Pinterest Reddit Email LinkedIn The president of the Republic of Moldova, Maia Sandu , said during an interview on Monday, August 17, that some Russian drones enter the country’s airspace by accident, but others are sent intentionally. The head of state was asked on the “360 Degrees” program on Teleradio Moldova whether the Russian drones that fly without authorization are tests of Moldova’s reaction and that of its neighbors. “I believe that some arrive by accident and others arrive because they are sent, and not only in our airspace, but also in the airspace of other states in the region. We have seen this in Romania and in Poland as well,” Sandu said. The drones “pose a danger to people, and the only one responsible, the only party responsible for these things, is the Russian Federation, which started this war,” she argued, referring to the ongoing conflict in Ukraine. Nevertheless, Sandu said that the expulsion of Russia’s ambassador-designate to Chisinau, Oleg Ozerov, would not stop unauthorized flights in the airspace of the Republic of Moldova. Official protests would be equally ineffective, she said. Instead, Sandu expressed support for “drastic” measures against Russia and support for Ukraine as the only way to stop the war. “The most important things that can be done to stop these drones both in the Republic of Moldova and in Ukraine, and everywhere, is to help Ukraine and for Ukraine to succeed in this war,” Maia Sandu explained. “We have seen throughout all these years that the Russian Federation does not care about protest notes." Dozens of incidents involving drones that entered the airspace of the Republic of Moldova have been recorded since Russia invaded Ukraine more than four years ago. Drone incursions have intensified lately, and a drone entered the airspace of the Republic of Moldova on Sunday, August 16, from Ukraine. It flew over Moldovan territory for 18 minutes and headed toward Galati, in Romania. According to the Defense Ministry in Chisinau, it was a Shahed 136 (Geran 2) type. The drone was shot down around 5 AM in Romania by an aircraft of the Spanish Air Force. Another drone reportedly exploded on Monday, August 17, in a field in Moldova, about 100 km from Chisinau. radu@romania-insider.com (Photo source: Inquam Photos/George Calin) Read next 17 August 2026 Defense Romania shoots down fourth Russian drone on national territory Normal Defense Russia intentionally sending drones to Republic of Moldova, president Maia Sandu says 18 August 2026 Radu Dumitrescu Like this article?
